real_qa.q: What safety changes did Targa Tasmania implement after the 2024 coroner's report on fatalities?
real_qa.r: The coroner's report contained 90 recommendations. Mark Perry stated they implemented many of these recommendations, though they believed some went too far while others didn't go far enough. The changes included the Targa Academy, speed limits, and modifications to course setup. Notably, the 2024 event was the first where no medical intervention vehicle had to enter a live stage to attend to a competitor.
real_qa.requete: Targa Tasmania 90 recommendations coroner safety changes

real_qa.q: Why did Targa Tasmania move from April/May to November scheduling after 2024?
real_qa.r: The event moved to November to keep the event on dry roads, which theoretically should make the event safer. November offered daylight savings and better weather. However, the move created unexpected challenges: more tourists, cruise ships, and traffic on the island in November caused significantly more disruption from road closures compared to the traditionally quiet April/May period.
real_qa.requete: Targa Tasmania November scheduling dry roads safety

real_qa.q: How many years was Targa Tasmania unable to run events due to COVID-19 restrictions?
real_qa.r: During the two-year COVID period, Targa only lost one event in 2020 (Targa Tasmania in Tasmania proper, due to island border closures). Despite this, Targa High Country and Targa Barrier Reef continued operating. Competitors from other states quarantined for two weeks in Queensland and another two weeks upon return home just to compete in the three-day event, demonstrating dedication to the Targa family.
real_qa.requete: Targa Tasmania COVID-19 2020 events cancelled closures

real_qa.q: When did Mark Perry become CEO of Targa Tasmania and what was his mandate?
real_qa.r: Mark Perry became CEO in 2006 under Octagon management. At that time, entry numbers were declining and the 15th anniversary event had been smaller than hoped. Octagon essentially gave him an ultimatum: turn the event around within two years or it would be closed. Perry successfully stabilized and grew the event, expanding it from a single Tasmania event to multiple events including Targa High Country, Targa West Point, and Targa Adelaide.
real_qa.requete: Mark Perry CEO Targa Tasmania 2006 Octagon two years

real_qa.q: What was the longest hiatus period for Targa Tasmania before its 2024 return?
real_qa.r: Targa Tasmania experienced approximately three and a half years of dormancy between the final fatality in the 30th anniversary event and the 2024 return. During this period, the business faced redundancies and commercial challenges while awaiting the coroner's report and recommendations before being able to properly plan the event's return.
real_qa.requete: Targa Tasmania 3.5 years dormancy 2024 return restart

guest.bio_context: Mark Perry was a spectator of Targa Tasmania in the 1990s before becoming a competitor in the 2000s. He suffered a serious neck fracture in a crash around 2003 and retired from competition. After working with Southern Cross and spending time at V8 Supercars as Director of Promoted Events, he returned to Targa and became CEO in 2006 under Octagon management, eventually becoming a 50% owner. He has steered the event through multiple crises including COVID-19 disruptions and tragic fatalities, successfully returning the event to running in 2024.
